name: core-ai/core-ai-map
title: Core AI Living Map
description: An interactive Core AI project map for a landscape iPad kiosk.

intro.default: Explore six open-source projects that help people and AI work with WordPress.

prompt.default: Tap to explore the living block map

default.name: Abilities API
default.description: A shared way to register and discover WordPress capabilities in a human- and machine-readable format.
default.technical: Abilities define inputs, outputs, permissions, and callbacks so plugins, people, and agents can safely discover and invoke site functionality.

default.name: Agent Skills
default.description: Reusable expert guidance that helps AI coding assistants follow modern WordPress practices.
default.technical: Skills package focused instructions for blocks, themes, plugins, APIs, performance, and security so coding agents can use current WordPress conventions.

default.name: AI Client
default.description: A standard, provider-independent way for WordPress code to request generative AI output.
default.technical: The AI Client gives plugins a uniform PHP API for models with different providers and capabilities, reducing provider-specific integration code.

default.name: AI Plugin
default.description: A modular home for user-facing AI features and experiments built with the Core AI foundations.
default.technical: The plugin demonstrates production-minded AI experiences while providing reference implementations that the ecosystem can inspect and extend.

default.name: MCP Adapter
default.description: A bridge that exposes eligible WordPress abilities through the Model Context Protocol.
default.technical: The adapter lets authorized MCP clients discover and invoke registered abilities while WordPress remains responsible for permissions and execution.

default.name: WP Bench
default.description: The official benchmark for evaluating how well language models understand WordPress development.
default.technical: WP Bench tests knowledge of Core APIs, coding standards, plugin architecture, and security practices to make model comparisons reproducible.

default.label: Create with AI
default.description: See how an AI-powered feature can use a common model interface and WordPress capabilities.

default.label: Let an assistant work with WordPress
default.description: Follow the path from agent know-how to a protocol bridge and an authorized site capability.

default.label: Build the WordPress way
default.description: Combine current WordPress guidance, a provider-independent client, and a working reference plugin.

default.label: Test what models know
default.description: Use a shared benchmark to assess WordPress development knowledge and improve reusable agent guidance.
